It does use a reveal (Lizzy and Martin's affair, discovered through a text message) to recast earlier scenes, and it ends on a thematic echo of Weil's idea of attention. Both are well-executed but familiar devices. There is no experimentation with timeline, perspective, format, genre or typography. Its strengths lie in characterization, imagery and theme rather than formal innovation.
